topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These introductory remarks outline the scope and learning outcomes for the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer interventions, cytotoxic chemotherapy, and drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional treatment modalities—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic drugs—along with their associated systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated resistance.

topics.label: Targeting cancer-specific vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic strategies designed to exploit intrinsic biological weaknesses of cancer cells, such as hormone dependence, checkpoint deficiencies, and synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Small molecule kinase inhibitors and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the design and clinical application of kinase inhibitors as well as the genetic mutations and bypass pathways that lead to drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapeutics and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the use of engineered monoclonal antibodies to target tumor cell-surface antigens both as direct receptor antagonists and as vehicles for cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relationship between the immune system and cancer, focusing on therapies that reactivate or re-engineer T cells to recognize and destroy tumors.

topics.label: Overarching challenges, historical progress, and future perspectives in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide a broad concluding perspective on historical mortality trends, current clinical hurdles, ethical considerations, and future directions across cancer care.
